card.name: Participles opening a reduced clause
card.fires_on: Past participles such as begun, shown, taken, drawn or been that start a reduced clause after a noun, with the verb 'is' or 'was' left out. They often follow a comma or a noun like 'Patients'.

modes.label: Participle after noun
modes.description: A past participle follows a noun and describes it, as if 'which was' were left out.
modes.example: Patients<< shown>> to have CAD and those with Prinz

modes.label: Participle after comma
modes.description: A participle follows a comma and adds a detail about the thing just named.
modes.example: colorized in gold,<< shown>> outside a white blood cell.

modes.label: Odd verb forms
modes.description: A participle or auxiliary appears with a missing subject or helper verb, in a list or in older prose.
modes.example: ●<< been>> confirmed to express the typical BCR-
